comments.text: I moved to Seattle WA from Dayton OH in 1995 taking my two young children across country driving through the west of the US.  We stopped for 2 days for a Yellowstone visit and I'll never forget how it felt...an ancient spiritual place that as I walked down to a creek there I looked up at the hills and could imagine seeing a dinosaur come over the hill.  Yellowstone has a presence if you slow down enough to feel her and get away from the crazy tourists.  It was something I'll never forget & the road through the park to our continued trip was on a one lane dirt & rock boulder edged clifts road that was scary as hell. ;)o  Wildlife everywhere - grizzlies as big as my little Honda Prius (from a good 300ft distance that is! lol)   Even traveling the highways I saw pronghorn in the scrub brush flats and it was so hot there in the summer we put sheets on the windows of the car.  We passed through other states but Wyoming, Montana, Idaho, and the Dakotas were memory makers for us city folks.  It is Big Sky Country for sure and spectacular to say the least.   I have been watching the videos of this channel and must say that even though it's AI narration the writing is spot on fabulous and weaves a wonderful visit with rich history and beautiful footage that sometimes makes me cry. ;)  Thank  you!

replies.author: @Kevin-j2d3u
replies.text:
You have to be the right type of person to live outside our towns. Personally, I have enough to do with chores to fill my day then sit on the porch or next to the fire ring in our pasture to watch the sun slide behind the mountains. If I need to, the drive into town is only about ten minutes. The drive to a WalMart or a shopping mall, about 90 miles. We know our neighbors but if we speak face to face more than five times a year that's odd. When a snowstorm buries our highway it may be 3-5 days for WyDOT to plow it so we all take our tractors out and clear enough that we can get to town or god forbid, the fire department or EMS can get out to us. 

If a stranger or a neighbor asks for help they get it immediately and without question. If the neighbor's cattle get out on the road, my wife calls them while I go out and start pushing them back inside the fence. I've had cattle I didn't recognize I pushed into my pasture until the Brand Inspector could get out and tell me who they belong to. 

A blizzard closed the interstate for five days Thanksgiving week. The folks in town opened a shelter at the fairgrounds. Local churches took turns making meals. A local diner, always closed for Thanksgiving, opened and served Thanksgiving dinner for the travelers. Free. 

In many ways we still live like the pioneers and we plan to keep it that way.
